assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy form one of the clearest bench-to-bedside arcs in recent medicine: the hormone's insulinotropic, satiety and gastric effects led to durable agonists that treat type 2 diabetes and obesity and show cardiovascular and renal benefit. The discovery is specific, the field changed visibly, and the impact on patients is very large.
assessment.attribution: Holst (native GLP-1 physiology and secretion in humans) and Drucker (intestinotrophic and proglucagon biology, translational GLP-1 work) are central to understanding the hormone; Knudsen led the design of long-acting acylated analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide). Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active GLP-1 peptide and Habener's work are contested or outside the supplied credit, so the allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of confirmation, large randomized trials and global clinical use make recognition timely, with the medical impact now unambiguous.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reward the hormone discovery or the drug development, and how to credit Mojsov and Habener (Habener is not in the supplied credit).
My recall of the priority disputes is from general knowledge and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, establishing a new therapeutic modality. The concept combined receptor engineering, costimulatory domains and clinical translation, and has spawned a field.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28-costimulated CARs, preclinical proof) and June (4-1BB CARs and the first pivotal CLL/ALL clinical results) are the strongest pair; Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified lymphocyte trials are foundational, though Eshhar and others are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: More than a decade of clinical follow-up, multiple approved products and independent replication; durability in leukemia and lymphoma is established, though solid tumors remain unresolved.
uncertainties: Omission of Zelig Eshhar and others from the supplied credit complicates a fair three-person configuration.
Safety (toxicity, secondary malignancies) and limited solid-tumor efficacy are still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Microbial rhodopsins used as genetically targeted light-gated actuators transformed causal neuroscience, allowing millisecond control of defined cell types and widespread application across systems, behavior and disease models.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) established channelrhodopsin as a light-gated cation channel; Deisseroth led the neuronal and in vivo application. Boyden, Miesenböck and Bamberg have strong claims, so a three-person limit forces difficult exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Twenty years of use with extensive independent confirmation; the tool is mature, while direct clinical translation is still early.
uncertainties: Hard attribution choice among six credited names.
A tool and method rather than a disease mechanism, which may weigh against it relative to other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed how the endoplasmic reticulum communicates with the nucleus to adjust folding capacity, a fundamental principle of cellular quality control that relates to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory-cell physiology.
assessment.attribution: Mori (identification of the signaling pathway in yeast, HAC1/IRE1 connections) and Walter (IRE1 mechanism, unconventional splicing) form a coherent pair. Other contributors such as Ron, Kaufman and Shamu may merit consideration.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well established and confirmed across organisms; disease-relevance is substantial but therapeutic translation remains modest.
uncertainties: Credit relative to Ron, Harding and others working on PERK/ATF6 branches is not covered by the supplied list.
Clinical impact is mostly conceptual so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defined the principal cytosolic DNA-sensing mechanism of innate immunity, connecting infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunology through a second messenger, cyclic GMP-AMP.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger and is the most decisive contributor; Barber identified STING. Vance, Patel and others not in the supplied credit also contributed, as did the STING-adjacent cyclic dinucleotide work.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly confirmed and highly cited, though therapeutic translation is still in early trials, so timing may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Boundaries of credit between cGAS, cGAMP and STING discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR is a central regulator of growth and nutrient sensing, with implications for cancer, metabolism, immunology and ageing, and underpins clinical use of rapalogs.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast; Sabatini identified mTOR and mTORC1 regulation; Schreiber's work on rapamycin-FKBP12 and the target is foundational. Brown, Sabatini and Heitman's contributions overlap, and Sabatini's later conduct may influence deliberation.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed, with long-running clinical use; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Attribution among Hall, Heitman, Brown, Sabatini and Schreiber is not simple.
Whether non-scientific considerations around one candidate would affect consensus.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chaperonin-assisted folding showed that proteins fold in the cell with assistance of defined machines such as GroEL/GroES and Hsp60, changing the understanding of proteostasis and folding disease.
assessment.attribution: Horwich and Hartl jointly demonstrated ATP-dependent chaperonin-mediated folding in vitro and in vivo; the pair is a natural two-person configuration, with Lorimer and Ellis also relevant outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed for decades; the discovery is mature, with possible concern that it is a classic fundamental finding with less direct medical impact.
uncertainties: Contributions of others such as Ellis and Lorimer are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic one, validating BCR-ABL-targeted therapy and establishing the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer treatment, including resistance mechanisms.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development and kinase program), Druker (clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms, second-generation drugs) form a plausible trio; Nowell, Hungerford, Rowley, Witte, Baltimore and others laid the genetic groundwork and are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of outcomes data; very mature, and arguably overdue from a purely clinical perspective.
uncertainties: Discovery-level credit for the BCR-ABL fusion lies outside the supplied names.
Industry-led drug development may complicate the allocation of credit.
